filename_mismatch.actual_paper: Markey-Towler 2018 - An Architecture of the Mind

title: An Architecture of the Mind: A Psychological Foundation for the Science of Everyday Life
classification_signals: No empirical data collection or methods section
Develops network structure theory of mind
Derives principles and propositions from first principles
Extensive theoretical apparatus with proofs in appendix
Conceptual model tested against philosophical and psychological literature
research_question: What is the mind, how does it function? Can we develop a mathematically logical and rigorous theory of lived experience that provides a coherent, integrated psychological foundation for understanding perception, decision-making, and behavior within the context of everyday life?

findings.antecedent: the mind as a network structure
findings.consequent: psychological processes operate within and are constrained by that network architecture

mechanism_chain.to_construct: cognitive constraints from network topology
psychological processes (perception, decision, behavior)

theory_commitments.theory_name: Network Theory (Graph Theory, Newman et al.)
theory_commitments.specific_claim: psychological phenomena arise from network structure of mind; uses mathematics of networks to formalize mind architecture
network capacity constraints affect cognitive processing

findings.quote: proposes a theory of the mind which is developed from the proposition that the mind is a network structure within which and upon which the psychological process operates

formation of internal perceptual representation

findings.quote: the vase and the faces... shifting perceptions of information in a context: the vase and the faces

mechanism_chain.to_construct: individual's perceptual representation (limited by salience)
cognitive analysis and comprehension
understanding constrained by information accessible through perception

findings.quote: the process of analysis: the individual forms an understanding g(H) subset of the objects and events H' subset of (v_x) contained within their environment

findings.consequent: individual selects action associated with most preferable implications through decision mechanism

evaluation against preference structure (aesthetics, values, judgments)
selection of action with highest preferability

findings.quote: identifying potential actions a_1, a_2, a_3... decision making, choosing the action a_j which is associated with the most preferable implications out of all feasible actions

findings.consequent: changing some incentive sufficiently will induce behavioural change through modification of action implications

change in relative preferability of action implications

findings.antecedent: information with sufficient salience (noticeability) and sensory impression on organs

mechanism_chain.from_construct: information in environment with inherent salience property
mechanism_chain.to_construct: sensory organs receive impression with sufficient intensity/contrast
perceptual representation activated in cognitive system

findings.quote: the salience property: if information has sufficient salience, 'noticeability', impression on the sensory organs, then the percept corresponding to it will be perceived

mechanism_chain.to_construct: network propagation along connections of sufficient strength
associated percept h' reaches activation threshold
conscious perception of h' follows perception of h

findings.quote: the follow-on property: if a certain percept h is connected by a relation R_rel of sufficient strength to another percept h', the perception of the former, h' will cause the perception of the latter, h'

findings.consequent: preference structure influences all downstream cognitive and behavioural processes through evaluation mechanisms

mechanism_chain.from_construct: network-embedded preference structure from accumulated experience
mechanism_chain.to_construct: access to preference values during decision-making processes
evaluation of action implications against preference structure
action selection, emotional response, and behaviour output

theory_commitments.specific_claim: preferences are properties of mind's network architecture; they determine all evaluations and downstream behaviours through systematic application

findings.quote: preference and value judgements arise and demonstrate their necessity for behaviour

findings.antecedent: social influences and cultural factors (rules, norms, expectations from others)
findings.consequent: psychological processes are modified through social integration of external rules into preference structure

mechanism_chain.to_construct: individual perception and salience of social expectations
integration into mind's preference and value structure through repeated experience
behaviour reflects internalized social influences through standard decision mechanisms

theory_commitments.specific_claim: social factors operate through the same mechanisms as individual preferences; social psychology is unified with individual psychology through network architecture

findings.source: Chapter 4: Reasons, Rules, Society and Motivation
findings.quote: social factors on psychological processes by revealing their role in and influence on mental networks

findings.consequent: environmental features influence perception, salience, and cognitive processing through their impact on what information is perceptually available and salient

mechanism_chain.from_construct: environmental architectural properties (spatial dimensions, visual complexity, design features)
mechanism_chain.to_construct: differential salience and perceptual availability of environmental information

mechanism_chain.from_construct: what is perceptually available and salient from environment
mechanism_chain.to_construct: formation of understanding constrained by environmental constraints on perception
decision-making and behaviour shaped by what the environment makes psychologically accessible

theory_commitments.specific_claim: architecture operates through perceptual and cognitive mechanisms; environmental design shapes what information becomes salient and psychologically available

findings.quote: churches? Certainly a concept 'available' to our mind... If the height of the middle building is taken as representative... they're actually within 20 meters of each other's height

findings.antecedent: mind operates as unified network with interconnected perception, cognition, emotion, and decision systems
findings.consequent: psychology and behaviour can be understood through unified theoretical system based on network architecture rather than fragmented discipline-specific theories

mechanism_chain.from_construct: mind as integrated network structure (not modular or fragmented)
mechanism_chain.to_construct: all psychological processes (perception, reasoning, emotion, decision, behaviour) operate within same network architecture
capacity to explain diverse psychological phenomena through single set of principles (salience, preference, decision, network propagation)
integration of psychology, neuroscience, economics, and social sciences into coherent Science of Everyday Life

theory_commitments.specific_claim: fragmentation of psychological science into disciplines is unnecessary; unified foundation can be built on theory of mind as network for understanding all human interaction and behavior

findings.quote: an integrated, holistic and systematic psychological foundation for the Science of Everyday Life... foundation upon which a view of human interaction may be built

limitations: Theoretical propositions not empirically tested within this monograph
Relies on philosophical and conceptual argumentation rather than experimental validation
Mathematical formalism (network notation) used but proofs relegated to appendix
Limited discussion of how theory relates to empirical neuroscience findings about brain architecture
Scope conditions for theoretical propositions not always specified
Some theoretical claims about environmental effects (e.g., P11) remain untested within the work itself
theoretical_strengths: Comprehensive attempt to unify psychology, economics, neuroscience, and social science under single theoretical framework
Explicitly articulates mechanism chains for key propositions (2+ steps required for theoretical papers)
Addresses fundamental questions about nature of mind and relationship to behavior
Proposes specific role for environmental/architectural factors through perceptual salience mechanisms
Network-based formalism provides mathematical rigor and potential testability

extraction_metadata.completeness_notes: All 12 major theoretical propositions extracted with mechanism chains. Book contains extensive appendix with formal proofs not separately extracted. Theory links and commitments identified for each proposition. Environmental psychology claims (P11) connect to architectural effects mentioned in filename mismatch.
